verdict.rationale: Anytype's own docs describe shared Channels with invited collaborators, so sharing a space for a project is documented. Nothing in the evidence describes simultaneous co-editing or how conflicting changes are merged. One older hands-on report said sharing wasn't available yet, which lowers confidence but doesn't outweigh the current first-party collaboration docs. Missing for 10: documented real-time or concurrent editing, conflict resolution or merge behavior, independent hands-on confirmation that shared editing works.

support.subject: As a researcher, I can share a vault or space with collaborators and edit notes together without stepping on each other's changes

citations.quote: a shared Channel for a project with collaborators
Anytype lets you collaborate with others without sacrificing your privacy.
You can even collaborate directly with others using peer-to-peer sync or self-host on your own network.
Collaborators don't need to provide an email address, buy a subscription, or ask anyone for permission.
